newsitem.title: UK: Dutch premier pledges to stay out of UK election.
newsitem.headline: Dutch premier pledges to stay out of UK election.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country has taken over the European Union presidency, pledged on Tuesday to stay out of the British general election campaign and find some way of working with Britain over Europe.

British Prime Minister John Major, who must call a general election by next May, was holding talks in The Hague during which Kok had been expected to press him not to turn the British election into an anti-European campaign.
The British election could be held only weeks before a June Amsterdam summit which is scheduled to agree landmark EU reforms ahead of the 15-member group's planned enlargement.

Kok said in an interview with Britain's Channel 4 television news that he had seen how New Year comments on the British election by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel had angered British politicians of all parties.
"I promised myself at the beginning of the New Year, at the beginning of our presidency, not to make on comments on how the British campaign should proceed," Kok said.

British political commentators have suggested that an mood of anti-European "Euroscepticism" may spread from Major's ruling Conservatives to the opposition Labour Party, which opinion polls say is well placed to win the election.
Kok pledged to push for progress before the Amsterdam summit.
"First of all, this is not a game of Great Britain versus the Netherlands," the Dutch premier said.

"We (will) see how far we can come. We in the Dutch government are not going to sit back and say, well, that's awfully sorry that for the time being we have a government in Britain that does not want to move.
"No, we will try to use our creativity to show our political will to find an opening for solutions," Kok said.
